name: Harbour and Piazza Core
tagline: The postcard heart of the village
description: The tiny harbour, the main street, and the little piazza where boats, cafes, and the Belforte tower meet the sea. This is the most beautiful and most crowded part of Vernazza, alive with day-trippers by day and quiet, glowing evenings once they leave.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want the classic view on their doorstep
pros: Steps from restaurants, bars, and the boat dock
The full postcard Cinque Terre experience
cons: Very crowded and noisy in high season

name: Upper Village toward the Station
description: The steeper streets climbing from the main drag up toward the train station and the road, away from the harbour crush. Slightly calmer and more residential, with glimpses of the sea and vineyard terraces, and a short walk down to everything the core offers.
bestFor: Slow travellers who want quiet nights but easy village access
pros: Close to the train for exploring the coast
Often better value than the harbour
cons: Steep stepped walks to reach it

name: Monterosso al Mare
tagline: The Cinque Terre village with a real beach
description: The largest and flattest of the five villages, one stop away by train, and the only one with a proper sandy beach and a resort feel. More lodging, more restaurants, and easier walking make it a practical alternative base while still hopping to Vernazza in minutes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a beach, more rooms, and flatter streets
pros: Flatter and easier to get around
cons: Still busy and pricey in summer

name: Riomaggiore
description: The southernmost of the five villages, closest to La Spezia, with steep colourful houses stacked above a small harbour. Well connected by train and popular for sunsets, it makes a lively alternative base with a similar look to Vernazza but its own distinct, photogenic character.
bestFor: Travellers wanting a lively base near La Spezia connections
pros: Excellent train links to La Spezia
Good range of bars and eateries
